description: Severe bone marrow suppression can occur.
mechanism: Allopurinol blocks xanthine oxidase, the enzyme that clears azathioprine metabolites.
management: Reduce azathioprine to about a quarter of the usual dose and monitor the full blood count.

description: QT prolongation and ventricular arrhythmia risk increase.
mechanism: Additive delay of ventricular repolarisation.
management: Choose another antibiotic or monitor ECG and electrolytes.

description: Torsades de pointes risk rises.
mechanism: Both drugs prolong the QT interval.
management: Avoid the combination. If unavoidable, correct electrolytes and monitor the ECG.

description: QT prolongation with a risk of torsades de pointes.
mechanism: Both drugs prolong the QT interval and amiodarone raises tricyclic levels.
management: Avoid. If unavoidable, monitor the ECG and drug levels.

description: Serotonin toxicity and seizure risk increase.
mechanism: Both agents raise serotonin and lower the seizure threshold.
management: Avoid the pair and review the analgesic plan.

description: Bleeding risk is additive across anticoagulant and antiplatelet pathways.
mechanism: Factor Xa inhibition combines with irreversible platelet COX-1 blockade.
management: Avoid unless there is a clear indication. Add gastroprotection when the pair is used.

description: Apixaban levels fall and anticoagulant protection may be lost.
mechanism: Carbamazepine induces CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein, accelerating apixaban clearance.
management: Avoid the combination. Choose an anticonvulsant that does not induce these pathways.

description: Apixaban exposure rises, increasing bleeding risk.
mechanism: Clarithromycin inhibits CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein, the pathways that clear apixaban.
management: Avoid the combination or reduce the apixaban dose as the product label directs.

description: Gastrointestinal and systemic bleeding risk rises substantially.
mechanism: NSAID platelet inhibition and mucosal injury add to factor Xa inhibition.
management: Prefer paracetamol. Ask the patient to report black stools or unusual bruising.

description: Dual antiplatelet therapy multiplies bleeding risk.
mechanism: Thromboxane and P2Y12 pathways are both blocked, so platelet aggregation is severely impaired.
management: Use only for a defined indication and duration, with gastroprotection in higher risk patients.

description: Aspirin loses part of its antiplatelet effect and both drugs irritate the stomach.
mechanism: Ibuprofen competes with aspirin at platelet COX-1 and both impair gastric mucosal defence.
management: Do not take ibuprofen with low dose aspirin. Separating the doses does not reliably remove the interaction.

description: Methotrexate toxicity risk rises, particularly at higher doses.
mechanism: Salicylates reduce renal tubular secretion of methotrexate.
management: Avoid regular aspirin with methotrexate and monitor full blood count and renal function.

description: Antiplatelet effect of aspirin is blunted and gastrointestinal risk rises.
mechanism: Naproxen occupies COX-1 and adds mucosal injury to aspirin antiplatelet action.
management: Avoid regular NSAID use with aspirin. Prefer paracetamol.

description: Peptic ulcer and gastrointestinal bleeding risk multiplies.
mechanism: Both drugs damage gastric mucosa and impair its repair.
management: Add a proton pump inhibitor and monitor for dyspepsia or melaena.

description: Clopidogrel antiplatelet effect is reduced, raising cardiovascular risk.
mechanism: Omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19, the enzyme that converts clopidogrel to its active metabolite.
management: Use pantoprazole or another proton pump inhibitor with less CYP2C19 inhibition.

description: Digoxin toxicity can develop within days.
mechanism: Amiodarone inhibits P-glycoprotein and reduces digoxin clearance, raising levels by up to 70 percent.
management: Halve the digoxin dose when amiodarone starts and check serum levels.

description: Digoxin levels rise with additive slowing of conduction.
mechanism: Verapamil inhibits P-glycoprotein and adds atrioventricular nodal blockade.
management: Reduce digoxin and monitor levels, heart rate and conduction.

description: Serotonin toxicity plus reduced analgesia and higher seizure risk.
mechanism: Fluoxetine inhibits CYP2D6, blocking tramadol activation, while both raise serotonin.
management: Avoid the pair and choose a different analgesic.

description: Severe and prolonged hypoglycaemia can occur.
mechanism: Sulfonamides potentiate sulfonylureas and impair glucose recovery.
management: Monitor glucose closely during the course or choose a different antibiotic.

description: Blood pressure control worsens and acute kidney injury becomes likely.
mechanism: NSAIDs block vasodilatory prostaglandins, reducing ACE inhibitor effect and renal perfusion.
management: Avoid regular NSAID use. Monitor blood pressure and creatinine if the pair is unavoidable.

description: Lithium levels can climb into the toxic range.
mechanism: NSAIDs reduce renal lithium clearance.
management: Avoid the combination. If unavoidable, check lithium levels within a week.

description: Methotrexate exposure rises, risking marrow suppression.
mechanism: NSAIDs reduce renal clearance of methotrexate.
management: Avoid NSAIDs, especially with higher methotrexate doses. Use paracetamol instead.

description: Peptic ulcer risk is substantially raised.
mechanism: NSAID mucosal injury combines with corticosteroid impairment of mucosal healing.
management: Avoid the pair if possible. Otherwise add gastroprotection and review symptoms.

description: Potassium rises and kidney function may fall.
mechanism: NSAID related potassium retention and reduced renal perfusion combine with mineralocorticoid blockade.
management: Avoid the combination. If needed, monitor potassium and creatinine.

description: Hyperkalaemia and acute kidney injury risk rise without added benefit.
mechanism: Dual blockade of the renin angiotensin system compounds renal and potassium effects.
management: Avoid combining an ACE inhibitor with an ARB.

description: Hyperkalaemia risk is significant, especially in renal impairment.
mechanism: ACE inhibition reduces aldosterone while spironolactone blocks its receptor, so potassium is retained twice.
management: Check potassium and creatinine within 1 to 2 weeks of starting or increasing either drug.

description: Lithium toxicity can develop within days.
mechanism: Thiazides cause sodium loss and increase proximal tubular lithium reabsorption.
management: Avoid or reduce lithium and check levels within a week.

description: Lithium levels rise, risking tremor, confusion and vomiting.
mechanism: ACE inhibitors reduce renal lithium clearance.
management: Check lithium levels and monitor for toxicity.

description: Potassium can rise dangerously.
mechanism: Angiotensin receptor blockade plus mineralocorticoid receptor blockade both retain potassium.
management: Monitor potassium and renal function closely.

description: Marrow suppression and mucositis risk rise sharply.
mechanism: Trimethoprim adds antifolate activity to methotrexate.
management: Avoid the combination and monitor the full blood count.

description: Sedation, respiratory depression and anticholinergic effects add up.
mechanism: Opioid and tricyclic central depressant effects combine.
management: Avoid in frail or respiratory compromised patients. Monitor sedation if used.

description: Sedation and respiratory depression become dangerous.
mechanism: Additive central nervous system and respiratory depressant effects.
management: Do not combine. If opioids are needed, titrate a single agent and monitor respiration.

description: Blood pressure control worsens and kidney function may deteriorate.
mechanism: NSAID prostaglandin blockade opposes ACE inhibition and reduces renal perfusion.
management: Avoid regular NSAID use and monitor creatinine if unavoidable.

description: Lithium levels can climb into the toxic range.
mechanism: Naproxen reduces renal lithium clearance.
management: Avoid the combination and check lithium levels if it is used.

description: Methotrexate exposure rises, risking marrow suppression.
mechanism: Naproxen reduces renal clearance of methotrexate.
management: Avoid NSAIDs with methotrexate. Use paracetamol for analgesia.

description: Serotonin syndrome and seizures are both possible.
mechanism: Both drugs increase serotonergic transmission and tramadol lowers the seizure threshold.
management: Avoid the combination. Watch for agitation, tremor, clonus and hyperthermia.

description: Rhabdomyolysis has been reported with this pair.
mechanism: Strong CYP3A4 inhibition raises simvastatin exposure many fold.
management: Withhold simvastatin during the antibiotic course or choose azithromycin instead.

description: Simvastatin levels rise sharply, risking rhabdomyolysis.
mechanism: Verapamil is a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor that raises simvastatin exposure.
management: Cap simvastatin at 10 mg daily or switch to a statin with a different metabolic route.

description: Bradycardia, heart block and hypotension can develop.
mechanism: Both drugs slow atrioventricular conduction and reduce myocardial contractility.
management: Avoid the combination, especially with reduced left ventricular function. Monitor rate and blood pressure.

description: Warfarin effect climbs slowly over weeks and persists after amiodarone stops.
mechanism: Amiodarone inhibits CYP2C9 and has a half-life measured in weeks, so the effect accumulates.
management: Reduce the warfarin dose by roughly a third to a half and check INR weekly.

description: Bleeding risk rises sharply. Aspirin also injures the stomach lining.
mechanism: Aspirin blocks platelet COX-1 while warfarin reduces vitamin K dependent clotting factors II, VII, IX and X.
management: Avoid the combination. If it is required, add a proton pump inhibitor and check INR more often.

description: Warfarin effect falls and INR drops, risking thromboembolism.
mechanism: Carbamazepine is a strong CYP3A4 and CYP2C9 inducer that accelerates warfarin metabolism.
management: Monitor INR closely and expect to increase the warfarin dose. Recheck after carbamazepine stops.

description: INR can rise within days and bleeding has been reported.
mechanism: Clarithromycin inhibits CYP3A4 and CYP2C9, slowing warfarin metabolism.
management: Choose a non-interacting antibiotic where possible. Otherwise check INR within 3 to 5 days and adjust the dose.

description: Marked INR elevation and bleeding during the antibiotic course.
mechanism: Trimethoprim inhibits CYP2C9 and the sulfonamide displaces warfarin from albumin.
management: Prefer another antibiotic. If used, reduce warfarin and monitor INR closely.

description: Additive bleeding risk with direct gastric mucosal injury.
mechanism: NSAIDs inhibit platelet COX-1 and damage the gastroduodenal mucosa on top of warfarin anticoagulation.
management: Use paracetamol for analgesia. If unavoidable, add gastroprotection and monitor INR and haemoglobin.

description: INR rises and bleeding risk increases during the antibiotic course.
mechanism: Metronidazole inhibits CYP2C9, the main enzyme clearing S-warfarin.
management: Reduce the warfarin dose pre-emptively and check INR after 3 to 5 days.

description: Additive bleeding risk with direct gastric mucosal injury.
mechanism: Naproxen inhibits platelet COX-1 and irritates the gastric mucosa, adding to anticoagulation.
management: Prefer paracetamol. If the NSAID is essential, add a proton pump inhibitor and monitor INR.

description: Bradycardia and heart block become more likely.
mechanism: Additive negative chronotropy and atrioventricular nodal blockade.
management: Monitor heart rate and watch for dizziness or syncope.

description: Simvastatin exposure rises, increasing muscle injury risk.
mechanism: Amlodipine inhibits CYP3A4 and raises simvastatin levels.
management: Cap simvastatin at 20 mg daily when combined with amlodipine.

description: Bruising and gastrointestinal bleeding become more likely.
mechanism: Fluoxetine depletes platelet serotonin and inhibits CYP2C19, adding to aspirin bleeding risk.
management: Monitor for bleeding and consider gastroprotection.

description: Bruising and gastrointestinal bleeding become more likely.
mechanism: SSRIs deplete platelet serotonin, impairing aggregation on top of aspirin.
management: Monitor for bruising and bleeding. Consider gastroprotection in older patients.

description: Atorvastatin exposure and myopathy risk increase.
mechanism: Clarithromycin inhibits CYP3A4 mediated atorvastatin metabolism.
management: Use the lowest effective statin dose or pause it during the course.

description: Amlodipine effect is reduced, so blood pressure may rise.
mechanism: Carbamazepine induces CYP3A4 and accelerates amlodipine metabolism.
management: Monitor blood pressure and titrate the calcium channel blocker.

description: Glucose can swing high or low unpredictably.
mechanism: Fluoroquinolones disturb pancreatic beta cell function and glucose regulation.
management: Monitor glucose during the antibiotic course.

description: Bleeding risk increases without a gain in benefit.
mechanism: Platelet P2Y12 blockade combines with NSAID COX inhibition and mucosal injury.
management: Avoid regular NSAID use. Add gastroprotection if the pair is unavoidable.

description: Digoxin toxicity risk rises when potassium falls.
mechanism: Loop diuretic induced hypokalaemia and hypomagnesaemia sensitise the heart to digoxin.
management: Monitor and replace potassium and magnesium.

description: Digoxin levels and potassium both rise.
mechanism: Spironolactone inhibits digoxin clearance and retains potassium.
management: Check digoxin level and potassium after starting.

description: Glycaemic control worsens during steroid treatment.
mechanism: Corticosteroids raise blood glucose and oppose sulfonylurea action.
management: Increase glucose monitoring and expect to adjust therapy.

description: Diuretic effect weakens and kidney function may worsen.
mechanism: NSAIDs blunt natriuresis and reduce renal blood flow.
management: Monitor weight, blood pressure and creatinine.

description: Hypoglycaemia is harder to recognise.
mechanism: Beta blockade masks the tremor and tachycardia of hypoglycaemia and can slow recovery.
management: Warn the patient that sweating and hunger may be the only warning signs and monitor glucose.

description: Insulin requirements rise during steroid treatment.
mechanism: Steroid induced insulin resistance increases basal insulin needs.
management: Increase glucose monitoring and adjust the insulin dose.

description: Thyroid hormone absorption falls and TSH may rise.
mechanism: Reduced gastric acidity lowers levothyroxine dissolution and absorption.
management: Check thyroid function after starting the proton pump inhibitor and adjust the dose.

description: First doses can cause a steep fall in blood pressure.
mechanism: Diuretic induced volume depletion amplifies the hypotensive effect of ACE inhibition.
management: Start at a low dose and review blood pressure and creatinine.

description: Lithium levels rise with a variable time course.
mechanism: Loop diuretics reduce lithium clearance and alter sodium balance.
management: Monitor lithium levels and hydration.

description: Lactic acidosis risk rises with dehydration or renal impairment.
mechanism: Diuretic induced volume depletion reduces metformin clearance.
management: Hold metformin during acute illness or dehydration and check renal function.

description: Metformin exposure rises modestly.
mechanism: Omeprazole can reduce renal clearance of metformin.
management: Monitor glucose and gastrointestinal tolerance.

description: Blood glucose rises and diabetes control worsens.
mechanism: Corticosteroids increase hepatic glucose output and insulin resistance.
management: Monitor glucose and adjust metformin or add temporary therapy.

description: Myopathy and rhabdomyolysis risk increase.
mechanism: Amiodarone inhibits CYP3A4 and adds its own myopathic effect.
management: Cap simvastatin at 20 mg daily and ask about muscle pain or weakness.

description: INR may drift upward a few days into the course.
mechanism: Broad spectrum antibiotics reduce the gut bacteria that synthesise vitamin K.
management: Check INR a few days into the course and adjust if needed.

description: INR can rise unpredictably during the course.
mechanism: Ciprofloxacin inhibits CYP1A2 and alters vitamin K producing gut flora.
management: Monitor INR during the course and again after it ends.

description: Starting or increasing thyroid hormone raises INR.
mechanism: Thyroid hormone accelerates the catabolism of vitamin K dependent clotting factors.
management: Check INR 1 to 2 weeks after a levothyroxine dose change.

description: Variable INR effect with added gastrointestinal bleeding risk.
mechanism: Corticosteroids alter clotting factor turnover and impair gastric mucosal healing.
management: Monitor INR and consider gastroprotection during the course.

description: Blood pressure falls further, usually as intended.
mechanism: Complementary diuretic and ACE inhibitor effects on blood pressure.
management: A common intentional combination. Monitor electrolytes and blood pressure.
